papers.title: Robust Bayesian Optimization with Student-t Likelihood
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization has recently attracted the attention of the automatic machine learning community for its excellent results in hyperparameter tuning. BO is characterized by the sample efficiency with which it can optimize expensive black-box functions. The efficiency is achieved in a similar fashion to the learning to learn methods: surrogate models (typically in the form of Gaussian processes) learn the target function and perform intelligent sampling. This surrogate model can be applied even in the presence of noise; however, as with most regression methods, it is very sensitive to outlier data. This can result in erroneous predictions and, in the case of BO, biased and inefficient exploration. In this work, we present a GP model that is robust to outliers which uses a Student-t likelihood to segregate outliers and robustly conduct Bayesian optimization. We present numerical results evaluating the proposed method in both artificial functions and real problems.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法可迁移至生物力学代理模型优化，但未涉及约束处理或FEA验证。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not handle constraints, lacks FEA or biomechanics application, and has no experimental validation in implant design.

summary_zh.method: 使用Student-t似然的GP模型进行鲁棒贝叶斯优化
summary_zh.result: 在人工函数和实际问题上均优于标准模型
summary_zh.validation: 数值基准测试与真实问题验证

summary_en.motivation: Propose a robust Bayesian optimization method that mitigates the negative impact of outlier observations.
summary_en.method: Employ a Gaussian process surrogate with Student-t likelihood to automatically down-weight outliers during optimization.
summary_en.result: The robust GP achieves better optimization performance on both synthetic benchmarks and real-world problems with noisy data.
summary_en.validation: Numerical experiments on standard test functions and real hyperparameter tuning tasks.

papers.title: Latent Gaussian Process Regression
papers.abstract: We introduce Latent Gaussian Process Regression which is a latent variable extension allowing modelling of non-stationary multi-modal processes using GPs. The approach is built on extending the input space of a regression problem with a latent variable that is used to modulate the covariance function over the training data. We show how our approach can be used to model multi-modal and non-stationary processes. We exemplify the approach on a set of synthetic data and provide results on real data from motion capture and geostatistics.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法提出了一种潜变量高斯过程回归，可建模非平稳多模态过程，但未涉及FEA代理模型或植入物设计问题。
llm.why_not_core: No demonstration on FEA surrogate modeling, no constraint handling, no uncertainty quantification focus beyond standard GP, and no application to implant or biomechanics design.

summary_zh.method: 在回归问题输入空间扩展潜变量，调制训练数据上的协方差函数。
summary_zh.result: 在合成数据和运动捕捉、地质统计数据集上展示建模能力。
summary_zh.validation: 通过合成数据及其实世界数据集验证方法有效性。

summary_en.motivation: To model non-stationary and multi-modal processes using Gaussian processes by introducing a latent variable.
summary_en.method: Extend the input space with a latent variable that modulates the covariance function over training data.
summary_en.result: Demonstrated improved modeling of multi-modal and non-stationary behavior on synthetic and real-world datasets including motion capture and geostatistics.
summary_en.validation: Validated on synthetic data and real applications in motion capture and geostatistics.

papers.title: Acetabular revisions using porous tantalum components: A retrospective study with 5-10 years follow-up.
papers.abstract: AIM: To evaluate the clinical and X-ray results of acetabular components and tantalum augments in prosthetic hip revisions. METHODS: Fifty-eight hip prostheses with primary failure of the acetabular component were reviewed with tantalum implants. The clinical records and X-rays of these cases were retrospectively reviewed. Bone defect evaluations were based on preoperative CT scans and classified according to Paprosky criteria of Radiolucent lines and periprosthetic gaps; implant mobilization and osteolysis were evaluated by X-ray. An ad hoc database was created and statistical analyses were performed with SPSS software (IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, version 23.0). Statistical analyses were carried out using the Student's t test for independent and paired samples. A P value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant and cumulative survival was calculated by the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: The mean follow-up was 87.6 ± 25.6 mo (range 3-120 mo). 25 cases (43.1%) were classified as minor defects, and 33 cases (56.9%) as major defects. The preoperative HHS rating improved significantly from a mean of 40.7 ± 6.1 (range: 29-53) before revision, to a mean of 85.8 ± 6.1 (range: 70-94) at the end of the follow-up (Student's t test for paired samples: P < 0.001). Considering HHS only at the end of follow-up, no statistically significant difference was observed between patients with a major or minor defect (Student's t test for independent samples: P > 0.05). Radiolucent lines were found in 4 implants (6.9%). Postoperative acetabular gaps were observed in 5 hips (8.6%). No signs of implant mobilization or areas of periprosthetic osteolysis were found in the x-rays at the final follow-up. Only 3 implants failed: 1 case of infection and 2 cases of instability. Defined as the end-point, cumulative survival at 10 years was 95% (for all reasons) and 100% for aseptic loosening of the acetabular component. CONCLUSION: The medium-term use of prosthetic tantalum components in prosthetic hip revisions is safe and effective in a wide variety of acetabular bone defects.

llm.relevance_to_user: 这篇论文是关于髋臼翻修术中多孔钽组件的临床回顾性研究，与增材制造生物材料方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve additive manufacturing (LPBF or other), mechanical testing, fatigue analysis, or surface characterization of biomedical implants. It is a purely clinical outcome study.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估多孔钽组件在髋臼翻修术中的中期临床和影像学结果
summary_zh.method: 回顾性分析58例髋臼翻修病例，使用钽植入物，基于CT和X线评估骨缺损
summary_zh.result: 术前HHS评分显著改善，10年累计生存率95%，无菌性松动生存率100%

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate medium-term clinical and radiographic outcomes of porous tantalum components in acetabular revisions.
summary_en.method: A retrospective study of 58 hip revisions using tantalum implants, with bone defect classification from CT scans and clinical scores.
summary_en.result: Harris Hip Score improved significantly; 10-year cumulative survival was 95% and 100% for aseptic loosening.
summary_en.validation: Clinical follow-up of 5-10 years with Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.
